newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian cricket team has thrashed England by 268 runs to take the third Ashes Test and level the six-Test series. Australia also scored their largest runs margin at Old Trafford, surpassing the 179 runs they won four years ago. Page 20.

Australian Rugby League national coach Bob Fulton has called for a united Australian team to tour Britain and New Zealand at the end of the year should there be a single rugby league competition. Fulton feels it would benefit the game internationally. Page 18.

According to Turner Broadcasting vice-president of sport Dave Maggard, Sydney and Brisbane are being considered as possible venues for the quadrennial Goodwill Games, to be held in 2001. Maggard is in Australia to scout both cities. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Socceroo player Matthew Bingley has joined Japanese team Vissel Kobe on an 18-month contract. Bingley's present club, Marconi-Fairfield, is expected to profit $500,000 from the agreement. Page 41

The Australian Rugby League judiciary has cleared St George captain Mark Coyne of a lifting charge, paving the way for him to play for the Australian side in the Rest of the World match in Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium on Friday night. Page 41

The Brisbane Broncos are expecting a financial loss of $500,000, despite the club's likely position as the most successful off-field performer in 1997. The final word on the financial situation however, will depend on the team's performance in Super League's premiership and World Club Challenge matches, which both carry a $1 million in prize money to be distributed among winning clubs. Page 42.
THE AGE

The North Melbourne Giants narrowly beat the Melbourne Tigers 94-86 in an Australian Basketball League match last night. The close game was only decided in the last two-minutes of play after Mike Mitchell broke a 84-point tie with a three-point shot. Page B8.

The hopes of the Australian women's under-20 basketball team were kept alive when they beat the United States 80-74 at a world championship match in Brazil. Chika Emeagi dominated play with 33 points and 13 rebounds to seal Australia's place in the semi-finals. Page B8

Soccer Australia is expected to have lost between $250,000 and $500,000 when torrential rain forced a 24-hour delay in the Socceroos' World Cup qualifier against New Zealand. Only 14,000, instead of the expected 30,000, spectators turned up for the postponed match. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League Tribunal has issued a three game suspension to Brisbane's Chris Johnson for pushing umpire Tim Shearer in last Sunday's match against Richmond. Johnson pleaded guilty to the charge and Lions officials will not appeal the suspension. Page 72.

Boom pacer Salinger put in an impressive workout at Moonee Valley yesterday, clocking a time that would have won all but three New Zealand Cups. The unbeaten three-year-old horse is scheduled for his first race outside Western Australia at Moonee Valley next Monday. Page 64.

Australian tennis players Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge made history at Wimbledon yesterday as the second ever team to win five doubles titles consecutively. They defeated Jacco Eltingh and Paul Haarhuis 7-6 (7-4) 7-6 (9-7) 5-7 6-3 to win $350,000 in prize money. Page 63
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Canberra Raiders secured second position behind the Brisbane Broncos in the Telstra Cup table after defeating Canterbury 28-10 at Bruce Stadium last night. Canberra gained a 16-6 lead at the break with three first-half tries. The Raiders will meet Brisbane next Monday. Page 68.

Merger talks between Super League and the Australian Rugby League for a unified competition continue this week with a meeting between SL chief Ian Frykberg and ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker. Discussion will focus on control of the game's finances an club resistance to the merger. Page 66

According to David Rofe, QC, an AJC committee member cannot also serve on the Thoroughbred Racing Board due to a potential conflict of interest. Rofe has proposed a controversial motion to ban such dual memberships which will be moved at an extraordinary general meeting of the AJC on July 17. Page 57.
